cards.text: The LORD of Hosts just finished calling out the priests for despising His name. Now the prophet Malachi speaks about all of them, himself included. He asks two easy questions, the kind where you already know the answer and you don't love where it's headed: "Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us?"

cards.question: Same Father. Same God. So what does Malachi ask why they keep doing to one another?

cards.text: Breaking faith with one another profanes the covenant of their fathers. Then Malachi stops asking and says it straight: Judah has broken faith, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem.

cards.question: Malachi says Judah has profaned the LORD's beloved sanctuary. How?

answers.text: By marrying the daughter of a foreign god
By building an altar to Baal in its courts
By selling doves and cattle in its courts

cards.text: Malachi doesn't go easy on this one. For the man who does it, he says, may the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob everyone who is awake and aware.

cards.question: Malachi says the man who marries the daughter of a foreign god is safe, as long as he brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts.

cards.text: Then Malachi brings up another thing they do. They cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning.

cards.question: The people of Judah are covering the LORD's altar with weeping and groaning. Why?

answers.text: The LORD no longer receives their offerings gladly
Their enemies have broken down the city walls
The rain has stopped falling on their fields

cards.text: Yet they ask, "Why?" Friend, that's me staring at a flat batch yelling "WHY?!" while the oven sits there. Off. Never turned it on.

cards.question: Malachi answers their "Why?" by saying the LORD has been a witness between each of them and the wife of his youth.
They have broken faith with the wife of their youth. Malachi says she is a man's companion and his wife by ___.

cards.text: Then Malachi asks, "Has not the LORD made them one, having a portion of the Spirit?" And right behind it: "And why one?" He asks the question AND answers it himself. I do that too, friend. Nobody else is up here to answer me.

cards.question: Malachi says the LORD made a husband and wife one. Why one? Because He seeks ___ offspring.
Since the LORD seeks godly offspring, Malachi tells the men they are free to send the wives of their youth away.

cards.text: Malachi tells them to guard themselves in their spirit and not break faith with the wife of their youth. Then the LORD, the God of Israel, speaks, and friend, I set the timer down for this one.

cards.question: The LORD, the God of Israel, names one thing He hates. What is it?

cards.text: The LORD of Hosts says the man who divorces his wife covers his garment with violence. Then that line again: guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not break faith.

findings.problem: The card says the LORD of Hosts just finished calling out the priests for despising His name. That fact comes from the passage before (Malachi 1:6-2:9), but it has no reference. The card cites only Malachi 2:10.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question doesn't read grammatically: "So what does Malachi ask why they keep doing to one another?" It also switches to "they", while the verse says "we" and card 1 says Malachi includes himself. No rule covers broken grammar or a pronoun shift inside a paraphrase.
findings.question: Should a choice card's question be rewritten when its grammar is broken, for example "So why does Malachi ask they keep doing this to one another?" becoming "Same Father, same God. So what does Malachi ask why we do to one another?" And should it keep the text's "we"?

findings.problem: Both wrong answers end with "in its courts" and the right answer doesn't, so the right answer is the odd one out. The right answer also uses the verse's exact wording, so it sounds more like the Bible than the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The story card runs to four sentences: "Yet they ask, 'Why?'" / "Friend, that's me staring at a flat batch yelling 'WHY?!' while the oven sits there." / "Off." / "Never turned it on."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card runs to five sentences: the first quote, the second quote, "He asks the question AND answers it himself," "I do that too, friend," and "Nobody else is up here to answer me."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to fill in the verse's wording, "He seeks ___ offspring." Nothing earlier lets the baker reason out "godly" over "many" or "strong". Both wrong answers are plausible guesses for the line's next word.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "I set the timer down for this one" doesn't land as a joke. It's unclear what setting a timer down means or how it connects to the LORD speaking, so a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
